name: 2123 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley, K12

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Nothing else read dates it, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the building's alley (east) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 35 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_35.jpg) at pixel (1172.93, 1332.64): the alley line by a median darkness profile over rows 1310-1355 (peak at column 1172.93; the building's alley wall is drawn on it), halfway between the north wall line (row 1301.26, a profile over columns 1145-1168; the lot line west of the building reads row 1300.0 on the same rule, so the wall is on the lot line to within a pixel and a half) and the south wall line (row 1364.02, over columns 1110-1160; the lot line west of it reads 1367.01, so that wall stands 0.56 m inside it), each peak refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_35_gcps.json): local E 1471.270, N -3679.108. The bearing is the parcel's, the draft's 179.318 less the half turn its plan frame took. The fit's own residual, 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this coarse copy, is all that is claimed.
placement.symbolic_location: 2123 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: east side of Prairie Avenue between 21st and 22nd Streets, parcel prairie_2123 (data/street_grid/1904.json); on the rear lot line, its alley wall on the alley's west line, its north wall on the lot line with 2115's, its south end in its own yard (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (toward the alley, so the building lies at negative u) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 1172.93) back to its west wall line (column 1098.99, a profile over rows 1310-1355): 73.94 pixels at the sheet's 0.185854 m a pixel, 13.742 m; and from its north wall line (row 1301.26, a profile over columns 1145-1168) to its south wall line (row 1364.02, over columns 1110-1160): 62.76 pixels, 11.664 m along the alley. A plain rectangle: the sheet draws no step, wing or porch on it. 2115's garage stands 0.43 m north of it (row 1298.92); south of it, 0.56 m short of the lot line (row 1367.01), is 2123's own yard.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-east corner, under its north wall line. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under a 30-degree roof dying into the north party wall over an open gable to the south; those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. No dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick. The small figures written inside its north and south wall lines are too coarse on this copy to read as wall thicknesses; the kit builds its own 13-inch walls.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the two storeys, the brick and the two window marks' places is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-2123-stable-1938. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, the label GARAGE, the alley wall on the alley line, the north wall on the 2115/2123 lot line (row 1300.0 west of the building; the wall reads row 1301.26, 0.23 m south, inside a pixel and a half) with 2115's two-storey garage 0.43 m north of it (its south wall at row 1298.92) and the key's fire-wall ticks on the alley line at that junction, the south wall free, 0.56 m north of the 2123/2125 lot line (row 1367.01 west of it), with 2125's yard beyond, one of the key's window marks on the alley wall (a cross with a dot for each storey, its strokes over rows 1329-1339) 6.08 m from the north wall, a second on the south wall (its strokes over columns 1137-1147) 5.80 m back from the alley line, a small cross inside the south-east corner, and small figures inside the north and south wall lines (not read). The alley is on the EAST, so the kit is turned to face it (alley_side east) and built in mirror image (mirror), as 2017's stable is (L-k12-2017-stable-1938), so that its party wall stands on the north lot line, where the sheet draws the fire-wall sign, and the open gable is the south end, which the sheet leaves free. On the alley wall, counted from the north party wall's inner face: a carriage bay 3.0 m clear under the loft hatch and hoist, the mark as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, and a man door with a loft sash over it toward the south end. On the south gable, counted back from the alley face, its mark as a stable sash with a loft sash over it. On the yard wall, counted from the gable end: a stable sash, a door and a stable sash, each with a loft sash over it, the door where the walk to the house meets the yard wall. The workyard is the kit's: a brick apron 2.4 m wide along the yard wall and a walk to the house's two-storey brick rear range (its rear wall at column 1066.89, rows 1320-1355) 5.97 m west across the back yard. The roof is the kit's gable with the ridge along the alley at 30 degrees, as 2031's and 2033's 14.7 m deep stables take, dying into the north party wall; no dormer and no ventilator, as the sheet draws none. No ramp, stair, lean-to, wing or range: the sheet draws none.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and loft are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: Sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building on the alley behind 2123, uncrossed, and letters it GARAGE. GARAGE is the 1911 sheet's word and is not read as the 1904 use (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11; the T-1842 census row s35-2123-rear backcasts the envelope and reconstructs the use as a stable/coach house). This record builds it as the house's stable and coach house: a carriage bay, a loft with its hatch and hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source read names a horse, a carriage or a motor car on this lot.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.

research_note: T-1938 refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the ninth of the package's alley buildings on the east side of Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street, to leave the draft (2109's and 2123's together, in one PR). The sheet census (census row s35-2123-rear, trace s35fp-2123-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 35 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle (12.0 x 10.5 m): the sheet draws a building 13.74 m deep from the alley line and 11.66 m along it, its north wall on the lot line with a fire-wall sign and 2115's garage just north of it, its south end free, and a window mark on its alley wall and another on its south wall. This copy of the sheet is coarse (0.186 m a pixel), so every reading here carries about a pixel. Nothing read dates the building before the 1911 sheet; that it stood by 1904 is the census's carry-back, which the district draft already made. No picture of the alley behind the 2100 block is known to this project; the Armour photograph solved for the house (T-3725) shows its front, not the alley.
